## Scope

Contracts: SIG-OPS-002 (production DB hard-to-lose: deletion protection, retain-backups-on-delete,
maintenance window outside scheduled batch windows, operator-set autoresize cap),
SIG-STORE-048 (ops/evidence buckets versioning + ≥90-day noncurrent retention), QA-7 (web bucket no
longer world-readable, serving via `sig-web` unchanged). Deliverable: one idempotent, reversible,
read-only-in-plan scripted production change under `ops/gcp/` — spec §56 requires the running stack
to equal `ops/` state, so the source of truth is the script, not a prose playbook.

## Design

One script `ops/gcp/protect.sh` on the house `config.sh`/`lib.sh` plan/apply skeleton:

- `--check` (default; `--dry-run` accepted): prints `PLAN:` lines for every planned mutation —
  `gcloud sql instances patch` flags, the lifecycle-file body per bucket, the IAM binding removal —
  plus `check OK`. No ADC, no network; asserts a code path, not live state.
- `--apply [all|prestate|backup|instance|buckets|iam]` (default action `all`): runs the five ticket
  mutations in the named order — AR-2 on-demand backup *immediately before* the first `sig-pg`
  patch → three `patch` calls (deletion-protection + retain-backups-on-delete; maintenance window
  SUN 09:00Z; autoresize cap 40 GB) → versioning + noncurrent lifecycle on the three buckets →
  `allUsers` removal on sig-web → post-state read + the same `--verify` evaluator + site checks.
  Each mutation is an atomic idempotent step: the script re-reads live settings first, prints
  `SKIP` when already in the desired state, patches otherwise, then polls the long-running
  operation and asserts `operationType == UPDATE`.
- `--verify [--from-state DIR]`: read-only outcome diff. With no flag it runs live `describe`/
  `get-iam-policy` reads (ADC-gated); with `--from-state` it reads recorded JSON — the exact
  mechanism the AC requires ("dry-run + --verify against a recorded JSON"). Prints
  `OK`/`DRIFT <check>: expected …, live …` per check; exits non-zero on any drift. Usable
  directly by the P35.3 probe as a real/nonzero eval.

Live-window guard (apply mode only; verify/prestate reads are always allowed):

- Refuses every mutation while `date -u` is inside the global 03:00–10:00Z batch band.
- `sig-pg` legs (`backup`, `instance`) additionally refuse inside the named AR-3 windows
  (2026-10-06T00:00Z–10-13T12:00Z, 2026-11-06–11-13, 2026-12-06–12-13, from the plan §8.4 backfill
  table) and while a `sig-materialize` execution is running (fail-closed if the check errors).
- Bucket legs (`buckets`, `iam`) may run inside AR-3 but never inside the daily band.

Restore point (AR-2): `gcloud sql backups create --instance sig-pg --async` — its backup id and
`operations describe` result go in this record before the first patch. Rollback per mutation:

1. deletion protection / retain-backups: `gcloud sql instances patch sig-pg --no-deletion-protection --no-retain-backups-on-delete`
2. maintenance window: `gcloud sql instances patch sig-pg --maintenance-window-any` (clears the user-specified window back to provider-assigned — the flag verified on gcloud 583.0.0; `--maintenance-window-day` accepts SUN…SAT only, no ANY)
3. autoresize cap: `gcloud sql instances patch sig-pg --storage-auto-increase-limit=0`
4. bucket versioning/lifecycle: `gcloud storage buckets update gs://<b> --no-versioning`; re-apply the prior lifecycle file (pre-state capture preserves it; today: none)
5. sig-web IAM: `gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding gs://…-sig-web --member=allUsers --role=roles/storage.objectViewer`

## Resume fixes (inherited work re-verified — what changed)

- `--verify --from-state` could not read the hand-captured pre-state file names
  (`bucket-sig-web-*.json`, `iam-sig-web-*.json`): the evaluator's globs only
  matched the script's own `describe.*`/`iam.*` names. `load()` now accepts both
  naming families; the recorded capture now evaluates (11 DRIFT — the true
  pre-mutation state) instead of 3 false "no file" drift lines.
- A bare ACTION (`protect.sh iam`) exited 64 though the usage line promises it
  is the default plan path — now parses as `--check` mode.
- Check-mode plan lines rendered `gs://-sig-web` (bucket names were derived
  from the empty project before `require_project` substituted the placeholder);
  names are re-derived (`_derive_names`) after the project id is final.
- Stop rules were report-only (exit on a non-`UPDATE` op / `/health` / site
  failure, rollback left to a human). The contract requires "roll that action
  back" — `_sql_patch` and the QA-7 leg now run the recorded inverse patch /
  `add-iam-policy-binding` inline before exiting; `act_iam` also takes a green
  site-check baseline first so "unchanged afterwards" is provable.
- `--lifecycle-file` replaces a bucket's whole rule set — the plan text claimed
  a merge. Now accurate, and `act_buckets` refuses (exit 7) rather than silently
  overwrite when a foreign lifecycle rule is present.
- `_wait_op` now returns non-zero (was `exit 5`) so the caller can roll back
  first; `act_backup` asserts the newest backup row is `SUCCESSFUL`
  (`ON_DEMAND`/`AUTOMATED`) before any patch may follow.
- Rollback for the maintenance window corrected to `--maintenance-window-any`
  (verified on gcloud 583.0.0; `--maintenance-window-day` takes SUN…SAT only).
- `WEB_TILES_PATH` verified live: `/tiles/sig_graph-sites.pmtiles` → 206 on the
  canonical origin (2026-10-02); now env-overridable via `SIG_PROTECT_TILES_PATH`.
- Test seam for the window guard: `SIG_PROTECT_NOW` pins the guard clock
  (both clocks echoed); the live `date -u` is always printed beside it.
- QA-7 rollback scope (found on the resume re-read): a post-check failure after
  a SKIP (`allUsers` already absent) called `_rollback_web_iam`, re-adding a
  binding the pre-state never had — a mutation outside the authorised list.
  `act_iam` now rolls back only when the leg actually removed the binding
  (test: `test_iam_leg_skip_never_re_adds_allusers_on_an_unrelated_outage`).
- Header comment claimed the SUN 09:00Z maintenance window sits "inside the
  05:00Z-12:00Z batch window" — G1-14/SIG-OPS-002 says the opposite (away from
  the 03:00–06:00 UTC batches); corrected.
- Five new stubbed-`curl` tests pin the QA-7 leg end-to-end offline: green
  path, post-removal site failure → rollback, still-public bucket → rollback,
  SKIP+outage → no re-add, red baseline → refused (23 tests total).
